title: Streams Module
definition: A core module representing a sequence of data made available over time. Streams allow you to read or write massive amounts of data chunk-by-chunk without storing it all in memory.
simpleExplanation: Imagine watching a movie on Netflix. You don't download the entire 5GB video file to your hard drive before hitting 'Play'. You download a tiny 10-second 'chunk', watch it, throw it away, and download the next chunk. Streams allow Node to read a 10GB file using only 50MB of RAM by processing it in tiny chunks.
realWorldExample: Uploading a 2GB video file to a Node server. If you use standard methods, Node tries to load all 2GB into RAM and crashes. With streams, it reads 64kb, saves it to disk, and repeats, keeping RAM usage near zero.

answers.question: What are the four types?
answers.answer: 1. Readable (reading data), 2. Writable (writing data), 3. Duplex (both reading and writing, like a TCP socket), 4. Transform (modifying data as it is read/written, like zipping a file).

answers.question: What is backpressure?
answers.answer: When a Readable stream reads data off the hard drive faster than a Writable stream can process it (e.g., slow internet connection), data builds up in memory. Backpressure is the mechanism where the Writable stream says 'STOP!', pausing the Readable stream until it catches up.
